title: Home Smoked Mackerel
ingredients: Freshly caught, home smoked Mackerel are the very best and cannot be
method: compared with any supermarket produce.
Simply arrange the, preferably still warm, fish some of our potato-salad, a few slices of
cooked beetroot, one large grilled slice of bacon, a few fresh salad leaves and some lemon
slices on each plate and serve.

title: A Garfish Recipe
story: Just for fun. Not that we will ever have enough garfish to cook this but I thought that it would be fun to read and could possibly be adapted for other fish.
ingredients: a few sprigs of thyme just the leaves
salt and black and white pepper.
method: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the onions until glassy but not brown, add the
tomatoes, garlic and thyme and cook for a few minutes.
Now pour in a large glass of the wine.
Taste to adjust the salt and add the two peppers, freshly ground of course.
Transfer the cooked vegetables to a casserole and put the garfish, with the head and tail still on it,
on top of the vegetables.
Cover with a lid or some silver foil.
Bake in a preheated oven at 170 for 20-30 minutes.
I think I would serve this with simply cooked potatoes sprinkled with parsley
and a nob of butter.
PS
I wonder if a few mushrooms and a red or yellow pepper could be added too.

title: Bass
story: There is simply no better fish than Bass. We use the simplest of cooking methods.
ingredients: some fresh Parsley and Fennel, a few slices of lemon
method: Clean and dry the fish and place it on oiled kitchen foil, transfer to an oven-proof tray.
Fill the cavity with: and salt of course. A little butter should also be added.
Now sprinkle some lemon juice over the fish and dot with butter.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180 for 15-30 minutes depending on the weight of the fish. Care needs to be taken not to overcook the fish. Bass can be served with new potatoes and a fresh salad.

title: Creamy Pasta with Salmon (1)
story: I found this recipe on a BBC cooking website. It is nice, easy and quick. For 4 people you need:
ingredients: 4 large salmon steaks cut into cubes
5 minutes or until the salmon is cooked
method: cook and drain the pasta, but while it cooks heat the oil in a frying-pan and add the onions, cook gently for 2-4 minutes only until the onions are glassy not brown ,now add the garlic and cook for two more minutes.
to this add cubed salmon and the double cream, lower the heat and cook very gently for
add the smoked salmon and heat through.

title: Creamy Pasta with Salmon (2)
method: Cook and drain the pasta
Meanwhile heat the oil in a frying pan add the onions cook gently for 2-4 minutes until the onions are soft, not brown, now add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
To this add the cubed salmon and the double cream lower the heat and cook very gently 5 minutes; or until the salmon is cooked.

Add the smoked salmon and carefully stir the salmon sauce into the pasta and lastly sprinkle parsley over the dish. Very nice if served with Frascati. I suppose this pasta dish could be made with all sorts of fish maybe even Mackerel or Pollack? The strong flavour of the socked Salmon will always help to improve the dish. In case Pollack is used I would add not 100 but 200g of smocked salmom.

mix the pasta with the salmon sauce and sprinkle with parsley This dish goes very nicely with a white wine, in my case it would be Frascati. Thinking about it I suppose this pasta could be made with all sorts of fish maybe even with Mackerel or Pollack. The smoked salmon would give some flavour, I hope, even to Pollack.

title: Seafood Chowder (1)
story: After having experienced the " delights" of this chowder in an, otherwise reasonable, restaurant I felt that I could very much improve this dish. So here is my variation. This is enough fo r3 or two very hungry people.
method: 1or 2 tablespoons of rape-seed oil and about 50g of butter
60g of smoked bacon lardons (do not use salt now but wait until the end of cooking time and see if salt is needed)
110g of peeled and finely chopped onion
1 heaped tablespoon of flour
400ml water
215-220 ml whole milk ( fat milk, blue top)
a bouquet garni made from a few stalks of parsley, 2 sprigs of fresh thymeand a bay leaf ( tied together with string and discarded after cooking)
800g of very firm potatoes maybe salad potatoes, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm cubes
freshly ground pepper and a pinsh or two of cayenne pepper
425g of mixed fish I used salmon and cod, cut into 3cm cubes
125-130ml of single cream
one or two or even three handfulls of frozen prawns To finish the dish sprinkle with parsley, serve with home baked Baguette and a nice white wine.

title: Seafood Chowder (2)
story: Begin by removing the skin from the salmon cut into small strips and just before serving fry in a little butter then place on top of the finished dish. (it's yummy ) Heat the rapeseed oil and the butter add the bacon and fry nice and brown. Now add the onion and cook "glassy". Sprinkle in the flour and cook, stirring all the time for about 2 minutes. Add the hot water (slowly bit by bit) and continue stirring, then the milk and the bouquet garni and cook for 5-8 minutes. It is now time to add the cubed potatoes, pepper and the cayenne pepper. Lower the heat and cook until the potatoes slip of the knife. At this point add you fish cubes and very gently simmer until the fish is cooked. Take the prawns out of the freezer and pour boiling water over to defrost, then drain and add to the pot. Heat the dish though and add the cream heat again. Serve with the baguette and plenty of good cold wine. This is a nice warming winter dish and for those very lucky people living near Borough Market it is so easy to find much better fish and a fantastic variety of shell-fish. Good luck, love Omi. PS There are very many recipes on the internet have a look for even better chowders.

title: A Very Simple Fish Pie
story: For the filling:
ingredients: 250g fish, I quite like cod/ salmon
method: about 100g of frozen peas
100g of frozen pawns, defrost in a sieve by pouring very hot water over
For the mashed potatoes:
Preheat the oven to 190
From now on it is all very simple.
Bring the milk to a "simmer" add the onion and the bay-leave and simmer again for about 5 minutes.
Take the pot of the heat and gently lay the fish into the milk mixture.
This will now have to "infuse" for 10 minutes or so.
Peel and boil you potatoes, drain and mash first adding the butter and the hot milk.
Next add half of the Cheddar and mix well in.
Gently lift the fish out of the milk and keep warm.
Reserve the milk for the sauce.
Melt the butter add the flour and then very slowly bit by bit the warm milk.
Like always the sauce should by nice and creamy.
I always like to boil the frozen peas in a little boiling water and then drain before adding
to the sauce.
Find an oven- proof pie dish and put a little of the sauce on the bottom followed by
the flaked fish and the prawns followed by the rest of the sauce.
Ladle the mashed potatoes on top and sprinkle with the rest of the cheddar.
Pop into the oven for 25 minutes and there you are all done and very tasty too.

title: Forelle – Trout
story: Forelle.......Trout
ingredients: A simple way of cooking trout. a little milk and water
2 nice and very fresh trout For the salad:
1 clove of garlic 1 small spoonful of sugar
some parsley chopped a small cupful
2 or 3 very small onions chopped of "Total" yoghurt
a hand full of porridge-oats a small fresh lettuce
one or two spoons of plain flour
method: For two persons you need: potatoes
a hand full of capers washed under running water I orange or 2 clementine
Start by bringing the peeled and cut potatoes to the boil then reduce the heat to a simmer
giving yourself time for all the other preparations.
Next dry the fish with kitchen-paper and cover with a mixture of oats and salt on both sides.
Melt butter in a frying-pan large enough for the two fish and gently lay the fish into the hot butter.
Reduce the heat and make your sauce.
This is like always .......melt butter add flour ....mix and slowly add the preferably hot milk
and water.....stir and when the sauce is creamy add capers and parsley.
It is very simple, but be care full with salt, make sure by tasting before adding salt.
Hopefully you have not forgotten to turn the Trout over!
Drain the by now surely soft potatoes add butter a bit more salt and warm milk and
mash.
Quickly make the salad.
peel orange and cut to small bits
wash and chop the lettuce
add some sugar to the yoghurt, stir, and mix in lettuce and orange.
Now it's time to serve............how difficult can it possibly be? :D

title: Shore Crab Bisque
story: Or simply crab soup This would serve four!
ingredients: 50g each carrot, celery and onions finely chopped plus one bay leaf.
salt and freshly ground black and white pepper
method: 1.75ml fish stock Tobias and Alexander sorting out the crabs. This is one of Rick Stein's recipes and only "slightly adjusted "
Cook the crabs in boiling water tip into a colander and drain.

Cop the crabs with a sharp knife or, and I find this far more practical, fill a portion of the crabs into a freezer bag and using a hammer or a rolling pin break the crabs in into very small pieces. Repeat this until all the crabs are chopped.

Melt the butter in a large cooking-pot and add the vegetable and the bay-leaf, cook for a few minutes but don't let the vegetable go brown. Try frying the carrots and the celery first and add the onions a little later.
To this add the crabs and the cognac and cook until the liquid has evaporated.
Now add tomatoes, tomato puree, wine, tarragon and the stock. Bring to the boil and then simmer for 30-35 minutes.
Strain the soup into a clean pan trying to press out all the liquid, and then pass it through a very fine sieve.
Bring the soup back to the boil and reduce a little to concentrate the flavour. Lower the heat and add the cream, cayenne pepper and the lemon juice.

title: Fried Mackerel
story: Fried mackerel are only good if freshly caught and should not be bought at a fish-monger. Dry the fish with kitchen-paper and dust in a mixture of flour and salt.
method: Fry the fish in a little butter and rapeseed oil.
In a separate pan fry some smoked bacon cut into strips.
Cut freshly baked brown bread and wash a few salad-leaves.
Arrange Mackerel on plates with bread and salad then put the bacon on top of the fish.

title: Salmon, Prawn & Samphire Risotto (1)
story: Salmon, Prawn and Samphire Risotto(1) This is a nice sea-food risotto with the advantage of ingredients easy to find in any supermarket. This will serve two. You need just:
ingredients: 50g of butter and 1 tablespoon of rapeseed oil
pepper and maybe a little salt
1 portion of samphire and 175g of Arborio rice
method: fish stock made from one cube, make a lot and use as much as you need.
cayenne pepper " to taste" maybe ½-1 teaspoon
also grated parmesan as much as you like

title: Salmon, Prawn & Samphire Risotto (2)
story: Salmon, Prawn and Samphire Risotto(2)
method: Prepare the fish by cooking it in a little water and lemon juice and salt in the oven at 160 for 15-20 minutes the drain and keep the liquid for later use. Keep the fish hot by covering it with silver foil.
Bring a pot of water to the boil and keep it hot for later boiling the samphire. It is important that no salt it added! The samphire is containing salt already.
Now make the stock using a fish-stock cube and adding the saved cooking liquid. Keep this stock on the simmer during all the time you make the risotto!
Melt the butter and the oil in a thick based large pot and add the onion and cook until glassy.
Add the rice and make sure that every single grain is covered with the fat and cook for a few minutes.
Start adding the stock now ladle by ladle but only if the first ladle is completely absorbed.

When you have used nearly all of your stock and the rice is cooked and nice and creamy you can add a small glass of dry white wine. Don't forget the risotto should be nice and creamy but no liquid should ever run out of it.
Quickly defrost the prawns by just tipping boiling water over and drain.
Bring the pot of water back to the boil add the samphire cook for 2-4 minutes and drain. Serve it in a separate bowl with a little butter on top.
Now flake the fish add this and the prawns to the rice and serve the dish straightaway. Never forget a nice cold glass of white wine!

title: Sherry Mackerels
story: Preheat the oven to 170 I found this recipe a very long time ago in a German news-paper and I think it is very nice and a change from the usual. Spread a little oil on the sides and bottom of an over-proof dish just big enough to hold 4 Mackerel. Rub a little salt inside the cavity of each fish also adding a little butter and lemon juice and transfer into the dish. Pour a cup of fish or vegetable stock over the fish followed by a large glass of sherry. Now chop one onion finely and sprinkle over the fish. Cover the dish with silver-foil transfer to oven and casserole for 25 minutes. Now take the casserole out of the oven, cover the fish with a generous layer of fresh bread- crumbs and top with grated cheddar. Put the dish back into the oven and bake until the cheese has melted and is light brown. Serve with freshly baked bread or mashed potatoes and a salad.

title: Mussels Moules Mucheln
story: Mussels Moules Mucheln "Mariniere " Before cooking mussels for the first time it is very necessary to take note of just three "safety tips". Buy mussels only from a supermarket with a good turnover so that you can be sure they are very fresh. Keep the mussels in the fridge and cook that day or, at the very latest, the next. When cleaning give the open once a little tap with a knife and if they then do not close discard them. After cooking it is the other way round. Do not try to open or eat the once that are still closed. When you are ready to cook give the mussels a good wash under running water and remove the "beards". The beards are the string-like bits that help the mussels to attach to the mussel-beds where they develop until harvested. And here at last is the recipe: I always think one sack of mussels is just enough for two.
ingredients: a medium glass of a very dry white wine
method: parsley roughly chopped
and of course about a litre of water
Melt the butter in a fairly large cooking pot add the onion and cook slowly until
glassy. To this add half the parsley the water and the wine.
Cook just for a few minutes and add all of the mussels in one go.
Put on the lit and shake the pot a few times. The mussels should cook for 3-4 minutes
and should all be open.
This is a very quick and easy meal and I think always lots of fun to serve for
friends and family.
My favourite thing is to serve it with freshly baked baguette plus some butter
and plenty of white wine.
Don't forget to sprinkle the rest of the parsley over the mussels just before serving.

photos.caption: One of Walter's very best meals!

title: Salmon with a Green Sauce
story: Salmon with a" Green"Sauce. This is my own recipe and the way I cook salmon most of the time. The sauce is a little unusual but is worth trying. The salmon is cooked in the oven at 180 sprinkled with a little lemon juice a few bits of butter, salt and a few spoons of water covered with silver foil. But wait with this until all the other things are almost ready so serve. There is no need for me to tell you how to make mashed potatoes or to cook a few vegetables. So I just write how to make the sauce. Chop one onion very finely and add to a sauce- pan containing some melted butter. Cook as usual until cooked but not brown. Add some flour and while stirring all the time keep adding some hot chicken- stock slowly and keep stirring until you have the usual "white- base- sauce." Now add some chopped parsley and cook for 5 minutes. Take the pot of the heat and add one or two teaspoons of capers ( fist rinsed with cold water) and a polish gherkin finely chopped. Now put the fish in the oven. And when everything is ready to serve reheat the sauce very gently. Enjoy with a light white wine. title: Bratkartoffeln
story: Boil potatoes in their skins let cool and peel the skins off. Slice into thick slices. This is best done the day before or in the morning if to be served in the evening. You need: Cold boiled potatoes cut into slices Smoked bacon cut into "lardons"
ingredients: butter or corn or linseed oil
method: Melt a little butter in a small frying pan and cook the onions until glassy.
Set aside and keep warm.
Fry the bacon in a large frying pan until nice but not too brown and add the cold, sliced
potatoes.
Fry until the potatoes are nice and brown on all sides, turning frequently.
Now simply add the still warm onions and the sliced gherkins and mix well.
And there you are, you made Bratkartoffeln all that remains to do is add salt and pepper
to your liking.
I serve the potatoes with fried eggs and a glass of dry white wine or some very cold Lager.
Very German and very good to eat, especially after work on a cold winter evening.

title: Cornish Pasties
story: By my late friend Eileen who was Cornish and grew up on a farm in Portscatho. Serving four
ingredients: 1lb skirt of beef cut into strips
¼ of a Sweet finely cut in to small strips
method: Filling
Rest the flour mixture in fridge for at least one hour.
Cut meat and vegetables in to strips.
Roll out the flour mixture and cut into rounds.
Fill the pasties and add a little Cornish cream
and salt and pepper to taste.
Moisten the edges of the pasties and fold
in the usual way and now brush the pasties with a little milk.
Bake at 200˚ for 15 minutes and then for 35-40 minutes
at 160˚ or until nice and brown.

title: Omi's Simple Chicken Soup
story: The cure for all maladies, especially for colds!
ingredients: 1 portion of chicken breast, with skin and on the bone.
method: This is almost too simple but also very quick and tasty.
Wash the vegetable and transfer to a large cooking pot,
add the chicken portion, with the skin on,
followed by a little salt and enough water to almost cover
the vegetable and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat and lightly cook for 1to 1 ½ hours.
When the chicken is cooked and the vegetable are soft
remove the meat and discard the skin and the bones.
Cut the meat in to smallish cubes and return to the pot
heat through and enjoy!
You can make Schwemkloschen to make the soup more substantial
or cook a handful of rice in a separate pot and after draining
add the rice to the soup.

title: Swemmkloeschen
story: This is a recipe for a very useful soft and tasty dumpling. I know it is very unusual but goes very well with chicken-soup and many other clear and savoury broth-like soups. You have, this time, to be very accurate with the measurements of the ingredients or the dumpling will not work! You need:
method: ½ teaspoon of freshly ground Muscat ( it is best to buy the nuts and grate those yourself)
measure the milk into a pot with a nice heavy base. and add the butter, a little salt and muscat.
measure exactly 70g of flour on to a plate.

separate 1 egg, keep the yoke and beat the white until fairly stiff. Now bring the milk mixture to the boil and then tip in all the flour in one go. Star whisking instantly and whisk until the mixture forms a big dumpling and comes cleanly of the pot. Transfer the mixture at this point to a clean bowl add the egg-yolk and keep whisking for about 2 minutes, then let it get cool. Add the beaten egg-white to the dough and mix well. Now form little dumplings (use your hands, it is fine to do so) and drop each one on top of your simmering Chicken soup. Give this about 5 minutes and serve. Just try this it's fantastic!

title: Potato Salad
story: This a very old family recipe and has been made by my family for a very long time, and I inherited it from my Oma and my Mum. I have to admit at this point to the fact that I do not have measurements for the ingredients and adjust it all depending on how many people are there for the meal. Usually it's about a "hand-full" of everything. The dominant fact is of course the amount of potato used. All other ingredients are adjusted accordingly. You need: salad potatoes boiled in their skins, cooled, peeled and thickly sliced
ingredients: a cooking apple, not peeled, and chopped into small bits.
a tin Anchovy fillets cut in halves
method: smoked bacon cut in strips and fried until nice and brown
a few capers if you have any in stock ( but in this case not a hand-full !)
Mayonnaise, I use the fat reduced mayonnaise and sometimes add a little
Greek yoghurt.
A few polish gherkins cut into slices give the dish just that little bit
of extra sharpness.
After preparing all the ingredients just mix it all together and enjoy.
By the way this is a very versatile dish and can accompany
cold /hot meat
cold/ hot fish......... and even hard boiled eggs.

title: Bacon & Stilton Risotto
story: Bacon and Stilton Risotto Serves 4
ingredients: 50g [ I think that it is not enough] of Stilton cheese.
method: 1.4 litres hot chicken stock
large handful of parsley chopped
Heat a large pan until hot, add the rice and toast for one minute
(-this adds flavour to the finished dish)
Gradually add the stock, stirring well after each addition and adding
another ladleful only when the previous one has been absorbed.
Continue until the rice is cooked.....this will take 15 minutes......[I think it will take a lot longer]
Meanwhile Cut the bacon in to small bits and fry in a pan until brown and crisp.
The bacon can be drained on kitchen paper! Better not to do it as all the flavour
will be lost!
Stir two-thirds of the bacon and parsley into the risotto. Check seasoning.
Garnish with remaining parsley and bacon and crumble the stilton over
the top.

title: Red Cabbage (1)
story: All my family, cooked red cabbage every winter to accompany all sorts of winter dishes. The cabbage freezes very well and can be made weeks in advance.
method: 2 cooking apples chopped ( I think if the apple is rather big one would be all that is needed)
Melt the lard or goose fat in a large cooking pot add onion cook until glassy
add the cabbage, cloves, cooking apple, vinegar, stock ( chicken made from a cub)
water and cook on medium heat until the cabbage is soft.
Now add salt and sugar and maybe some more vinegar or if you like red wine.
So far so good!
Then one day I found a recipe by a" famous" cook and it had a lot of very
interesting ingredients.
So far so good.

title: Red Cabbage (2)
story: Then one day I found a recipe by a famous cook and this had a lot of other ingredients. A little cinnamon, a little nutmeg, one clove of garlic and a little brown sugar................... and so I tried a little of this with good results. In the end it comes down to a lot of tasting and then you decide when it is just right.

title: Tomato & Rice Soup
story: Tomato and Rice Soup You need:
ingredients: 2 sticks of celery also finely chopped
a little sugar a little lemon juice
salt and freshly ground white pepper
method: Start by boiling any rice you like, long-grain, basmati,
wild, brown or a mixture in boiling salted water and drain.
Heat a little oil in a large saucepan and add the onion, carrot, and
celery then cook gently until the vegetables are soft.
Add a teaspoon of sugar and the tomato puree
followed by the tin of chopped tomatoes and the of vegetable stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes and adjust the flavour by adding some lemon juice
and if needed salt and pepper.
Like always add a bit of this or that until you feel it is right.
Mix the cooked and drained rice into the soup and reheat.
Just before serving sprinkle with chopped parsley.

title: Pizza
story: Pizza Pizza Pizza Pizza Pizza Pizza Pizza ........................ At last I have found a perfect way of making pizza- dough. Gone are the days of " Yeasty, bready" dough. From now on all is well and I will try this out on everybody, there will be no escape........................ ! To be honest I found this on the BBC food website and really think that this is the fastest and easiest way of making a Pizza. Preheat the oven to 220 and put 2 baking trays in to heat up. For the sauce:
ingredients: 1-2 cloves of garlic and I also use a small onion
method: 1 teaspoon of dried mixed herbs and I also add a few sprigs of fresh thyme
Gently cook the chopped onion and the crushed garlic in a little oil until tender.
Add the tomatoes the herbs the sugar a little salt and some freshly ground black pepper
and simmer everything for 10-15 minutes. Leave this to cool completely.
You can make this sauce the day before and keep it covered with cling-film.
For the dough:
To make the dough is very easy.............
Mix the flour with the salt and the baking powder add the yoghurt and mix!
Do this with a fork not a spoon.
When the mixture forms rough dough turn it out on a floured work surface and
knead to form a smooth ball.
Divide the dough and rollout each one into a thin circle.
Be careful when removing the very hot baking trays from the oven and lay the pizza
bases on the trays. Bake for 3-4 minutes until the pizza bases are beginning to rise.
Remove the trays and turn the pizza bases over and top with the sauce.
Now you can top this with your favourite toppings.
Season with black pepper and return to the oven for about 5 minutes.
Serve with a green salad and a glass of cold wine.

title: Leek & Potato Soup
story: Leek and Potato Soup
ingredients: 600g leeks washed and cut into thick slices
salt and freshly ground white pepper
method: Parmesan cheese freshly grated to serve.
Melt butter over a low heat and stir in leek, onions cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Now add the potatoes and 750ml stock bring to a boil, lower heat and simmer
for 20 to 30 minutes or until the potatoes are soft.
Transfer to a food-processor and process to a puree, reheat.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle into dishes and drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with parsley and parmesan
Serve with buttered bread or better with freshly baked baguette.

title: Hot 3 Bean Salad
story: This is a hot bean salad suitable for a light evening meal served with nice crisp baguette, and is also one of Tobias's old favourites.
ingredients: 1 tin of Borlotti or Cannellini beans
6 slices of smoked bacon cut into strips or "lardons"
1 onion peeled and finely sliced / 2 garlic cloves crushed
freshly ground black pepper and salt
method: Cook the green beans in salted boiling water until tender and drain. Wash the canned tinned beans
under running cold water and drain.
Meanwhile fry the bacon until brown and add the onion and fry until glassy and for the last two
minutes add the garlic. Now sprinkle the flour over the bacon and onion and when it is absorbed
add hot water stirring all the time until you have a nice creamy gravy. Add a little lemon juice
and salt and pepper to taste followed by all the beans and heat through.
To finish sprinkle a little parsley over the top.

title: Puy Lentil Soup with Spinach
story: By Nigel Slater This is enough for 4 as a light evening meal.
ingredients: a good handful of unsmoked bacon
method: olive or rape-seed oil
(I think smoked is much better.... Sorry Nigel)
stock or water enough to cover the lentils completely
I sometimes use frozen spinach, not quite correct but it will do.
In this case you have, of course, to cook the spinach according to instructions.
I am afraid I have rewritten the method of how to cook this dish, simply because Nigel
makes rather a drama of the way he writes his instructions.
So here is the simpler way....................
Fry the bacon and add the onions when the bacon is nice and brown
followed by the garlic and the parsley.
Wash the lentils and add to the bacon mixture followed by the stock
or water and the bay leaf.
Bring to the boil then turn down the heat and simmer roughly
for 30 minutes. My tip is simply to try now and again and simmer until
the lentils are soft. Taste for salt and pepper and add some lemon juice.
Now cook the spinach, after washing it if needed, by adding a tablespoon of water to the
pot of spinach put the lid on and after a few minutes when it.
has wilted drain all the liquid out of the pot.
Now put some of the spinach in each soup-plate and ladle the lentils
over the spinach.
Serve the soup with baguette and maybe a little selection of cheese.

title: Spaghetti ala Carbonara
story: To serve 4 people you need:
ingredients: 200g of smoked bacon cut into strips including the fat
some olive oil and a little butter
method: and about 100ml double cream or may be just a bit more
cook the pasta
heat a frying pan until very hot add the oil and butter and fry the bacon until nice and brown
mix the cream and 3 of the eggs + 1 egg yolk to make a creamy sauce
drain the pasta and mix it well with the hot bacon and all the fat remaining in the pan

Immediately mix the egg-sauce and ¾ of the cheese into the hot pasta sprinkle the remaining cheese over the meal and mill lots of black pepper on top. It needs to be black pepper for the "Carbonara " effect!

title: Pfannkuchen Pancakes
ingredients: a spoon-full or two of cherry-pie filling and vanilla ice-cream
method: about ½ litre of milk
Mix the flour, the egg yolks, salt and some or all of the milk to make a batter of a
not to thin consistency.
Cover the bowl with cling-film and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Beat the egg-whites until fairly stiff and mix carefully into the batter making
sure that you not louse too much of the air from the egg-whites.
Now heat the pan and when you think it is quite hot add a little of the butter.
The fat should be very hot but not quite smoking.
Next ladle some of the batter into the pan and fry the pan-cake nice and brown on both
sides. I know this will take a little practise but you will get there in the end.
When all the batter is used up fill your pancakes with anything you like from
Savoury to sweet.
How about:
nice brown smoked bacon
or grated cheese
or cut up "Rollmops"( Pickled herring) Really nice mixed with a bit of plain Greek yoghurt
or even a few cut-up slices of German Salami mixed with a bit of Dijon mustard.
Or all sweet of course
or simply lemon juice and sugar
or cut up tined peaches mixed with custard
Whatever you like!

title: Arni Psito – The Greek
story: Better known as "The Greek" For two you need:
ingredients: 4-5 large potatoes, peeled and cut into quarters
5-6 medium tomatoes, skinned and cut into large slices
a kitchen-knife peel the tomatoes and cut into sick slices.
method: Heat the oven to 190
This is one of the simplest meals, very quick and easy.
Just put the potatoes first on the bottom of an ovenproof casserole
and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Now lay the meat on top and sprinkle with lemon juice and again
add salt and pepper.
For the tomatoes I recommend that you first put all the tomatoes
into a heat-proof dish, and then pour in enough boiling water to cover the tomatoes completely.
After just a few minutes tip the water out and with the help of a fork and
To finish the dish lay the tomatoes on top of the meat, and again, add a little
lemon and salt and pepper.
Lastly add a little corn-oil and a cup of cold water.
Casserole for one and a half, to two hours.

title: Lambs Liver
story: Lambs liver is the very best. It is soft and full of flavour. This will serve two.
ingredients: a little milk and continue to cook for a few minutes.
method: 3 or 4 slices of liver
1 large onion and some garlic
¾ of a pound of mushrooms
a small pot of single cream
long grained rice

green salad leaves Chop up all the ingredients taking care with the liver; it needs to be cut into very thin little strips. Melt a little butter in a large pan and add onions and a little later the garlic. Cook on a low heat for about 10 minutes now add the mushrooms cook this again for 10 minutes. Drain the cooking liquid into a jug and set the vegetables aside. Melt butter in a pan and when it is melted add a little, 2-3 teaspoons plain flour. As soon as the flour and the butter are combined start adding the mushroom liquid stirring all the time. This sauce should be nice and creamy. If it appears too thick add At this point add the mushrooms and a little single cream if you like. By now the rice, having been cooked in boiling salted water, should be ready and drained and the salad ready to serve. Now, to the last and most important part. Heat some butter and rapeseed oil in a large frying-pan taking care to get it very hot and add the liver slices. Fry the liver only for a few seconds. If you cook it longer it will get hard and the whole meal will be spoiled! Lastly add the liver to the mushroom sauce and serve the meal quickly.

title: Lamb Steak a la Greek
story: This slightly, or better nearly, Greek meal reminds me of what is very often served in Germany's "Greek" restaurants! This serves two, just increase the ingredient and serve it to lots of people. For the Humus:
ingredients: ½ cucumber peeled and finely grated
2 garlic cloves grated or pressed through a garlic-press
a little lemon juice to taste
2 large lamb steaks or maybe 4 lamb chops
method: lemon juice
Put all the ingredients in a blender cream together and adjust the lemon and salt to your taste.
For the Tzatziki :
150g Greek yoghurt ( the fat variation) I use "Totall"it is the best and very creamy.
First put the peeled and finely grated cucumber into a little bowl sprinkle with salt and wait for 10-
15 minutes then, using your hands, squeeze all the liquid that has formed completely out of the
cucumber.
Put the cucumber into a bowl and add all the other ingredients and stir this until well mixed.
For the salad: you need fresh green salad leafs
olive oil, lemon juice, white pepper and salt as well as a crushed garlic clove to make
this into a very nice salad.
Next heat the oven to the temperature recommended on the" Ready to bake"
baguettes and heat the grill to a very high temperature.
brush the meat with a mixture of olive oil and crushed garlic.
When the Salad, Tzatziki and Hummus are ready put the baguettes in the oven and bake
according to the time given.
Brush the meat with olive oil and garlic and put under the grill.
Grill the meat on both sides for 2-4 minutes. ( It all depends of course on the meat and how you
like it done)
I serve all this together and open a bottle of Retsina but also always a bottle of Frascati
for those that cannot stand the taste of the rather unusual Greek Retsina.

title: Roast Chicken
story: Roast Chicken. Goose, Duck, and Turkey. Roasting any of those is very easy and just looks complicated but quite impressive when the meal is finally served. But let's start with the chicken. A chicken of 1 ½ kg needs to roast for about 1 hour 15 minutes, the first hour at 180, and the last 15 minutes or so at 200 to give the chicken a nice brown finish. There is one golden rule. When you think that the chicken is cooked insert a sharp fork into the leg of the Chicken and if the juices run clear then the chicken is cooked and you can give it it's last
ingredients: 15 minutes to get it nice and brown.
1 onion and 1 cooking apple both cut into chunks
a little flour/ a little butter
method: It is very important that poultry is cook really well and thoroughly!
If you like to cook it the way I do, then you need:
very strong " Hot!" curry powder
long grained rice
water
green vegetables or just a nice salad
Preheat the oven
Mix the onion, apple and lemon with some white pepper and a little salt.
Stuff the chicken with this mixture and transfer to a roasting tin. If you have made too much of the
stuffing that is just fine and you can sprinkle it around the chicken.
Now, and this is very important, add a cup full of cold water to the tin, cover with tin-foil
and start roasting.
You have now plenty of time to cook the rice, simply in salted boiling water, and prepare
the vegetables or the salad.
When you think the chicken is cooked remove it from the oven, lift the chicken out of the tin
and drain the liquid into a jug. Put the chicken back in the tin and back into the oven, turn up
the heat and roast for the last 15 minutes. But this time do not cover it with the foil.
Now make the curry sauce.
Ladle a few teaspoons of the curry powder into a cup add a little water and mix this
into a paste. How much of the powder you use depends on how "hot" you
like your gravy.
Melt the butter in a cooking pot and add a little flour, mix well.
When the butter has absorbed the flour start adding the reserved cooking juices
stirring of the time until you have a nice creamy gravy.
Now add you curry-paste, some salt and stir well, cook this for 2-3 minutes on a low setting
and taste to see if more curry powder is needed.
Now all that remains to do is drain the rice, finish your salad, take the chicken out
and serve. Don't forget to cool a bottle of white wine!

title: Lamb Casserole with Apricots
story: Easy to make and very good to eat. This casserole serves four.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons of rapeseed or corn oil
a few spring of fresh thyme
one or two handfuls of apricots
method: black pepper
(I buy the once that are vacuum packed
in this case no soaking overnight is needed)
Dust the meat with four, shaking off any surplus, then fry in very hot
oil and butter until brown.
Transfer to an oven-proof casserole.
Fry the carrots in the remaining fat after 15 minutes, add the onions
and fry for 10minutes or so and for the last few minutes of frying
add the garlic.
All is added to the meat in the casserole followed by the thyme and
the bay-leaf.
At this point pour in some boiling water, but do not cover the meat and
vegetable completely.
Don't forget a little salt and some freshly ground pepper.
I use both white and black pepper.
Cook the casserole at 160-170 for 11/2- 2 hours, towards the end
of cooking time lay the apricots and top of the stew and replace
the lid again and casserole for another 15 minutes.
Serve this meal with freshly baked baguette and green vegetables.

title: Grune Kohl / Curly Kale
story: For one person you need:
ingredients: 1 loin of pork, a small one will do
½ of a French sausage ...Jean Caby "La Seche"
1 hand full of porridge oats is also needed.
method: but if this is not possible I used
a mature French dry pork sausage with the white skin peeled off and cut into cubes.
German Mettwurst is also possible as a last resort.
Don't be tempted to use any other sausage, like Chorizo the end result would not be the
traditional North German dish, which comes by the way from my father's side of the
family.
Dijon mustard
and lastly 1 onion
Start with peeling and chopping the onion.
Melt a table spoon of butter in a in a large cooking pot add the onion and
cook over a low heat until the onion is getting "glassy," definitely not brown.
Now add all the meats and cover with boiling water and over a medium heat
cook for ½ an hour.
Now add the washed and chopped up kale, keep the heat medium and
cook for about 1 ½ to 2 hours.
Just 15 minutes before the end of the cooking time add the oats.
This dish will improve in flavour if it is cooked a day ahead and kept
at room temperature.
Just reheat it the next day and serve with roasted potatoes.
I usually serve this meal with cold Lager and have a pot of Dijon mustard
on the table.

title: Eier, Lamb & Chicken Fricassee
story: Fricassee can be made from almost any rest of meat but in case of chicken-fricassee the chicken is usually cooked just for this meal in water with a few vegetable and salt added and then cut into portion. But it is also possible to just make the sauce and add some hard-boiled eggs. This is a meal that Bias liked very much and really just consists of a white sauce made more interesting by adding different flavours. So here is the basic recipe: I onion chopped
ingredients: a few mushrooms cooked in butter
a few fillets of Anchovy cut in to small bits
a teaspoon or two of capers
method: stock made from a cube, but if you cook a chicken use the cooking-liquid!
So now melt the butter add the onion and when the onion is cooked but not brown
add the flour stirring all the time and slowly add the liquid until you have a nice and
creamy white sauce. Now, and this is important, add a little lemon juice to taste
making a simple white sauce into a "Fricassee sauce".
Do not let the sauce boil after this, just gently reheat.
From now on anything goes. You can add:
a small tin of drained peas or frozen peas cooked before of course
How much of this or the combination you use is up to you.
Gently reheat the sauce again and pour over the meat or the eggs.
I serve this meal with boiled white and very delicious black rice plus a simple summer salad.

title: Sausages & Mashed Potatoes
story: Sausages and mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 6 good sausages any variety really, but I recommend a strongly
butter and milk for the potatoes
a small glass Marsala or Sherry for the gravy
½ vegetable stock cube to make the stock
one or two teaspoons of flour for the gravy
method: flavoured sausage.
also needed are a few juniper berries , thyme leaves and one or two bay leaves
Set the oven to 150.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan and brown the sausages on all sides and transfer
to an ovenproof dish.
Add the sliced onions to the frying pan, lower the heat and fry very gently until cooked.
This can take up to 20 minutes or more take care not to get the onions too dark.
At this point if the onions are looking too pale use a little gravy browning, this is
much better then running the risk of letting the onions burn and become bitter.
Now add the crushed juniper berries, bay leaf, and thyme.
When the onions look nice cooked mix in the flour and slowly pour
in the stock and the Marsala. Let it all come to the boil, and stirring all the time,
wait until the gravy thickens.
Season with salt and pepper, if needed, and add some Dijon mustard.
Pour the onion sauce over the sausages and transfer to the oven.
Cook for 20-25 minutes.
Having made the mach by now just serve the meal with cold Frascati.

title: Irish Stew
story: You need:
method: potatoes
butter or lard and a teaspoon of caraway seeds plus salt and pepper.
Shred the cabbage finely and peel and cube the potatoes.
Slice the onion and fry in a little butter until cocked but not brown.
Crush the garlic, about two cloves.
Brush some corn-oil on the inside of a casserole and layer the ingredients starting
with the potatoes, then some of the meat followed, the onion and so on.
Don't forget to add a little caraway, salt and pepper between the layers.
Add some water, about 1-2 cups.
Casserole the dish at 180 for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
This is a very nice and warming winter dish!

title: Venison / Pheasant Casserole
ingredients: 1 kg of venison cut into cubes and pheasant cut into portions.
a little butter and corn oil
a good handful of smoked bacon cut into lardons
2 handfuls of mushrooms cut in half
salt and freshly ground white and black pepper
method: This recipe can be used for just pheasant or just venison or as a combination of both.
good red wine and some water
Preheat
Oven to
Fry the bacon in a mixture of butter and vegetable oil until nice and brown add the onions and when
those are glassy but not brown add the garlic and fry at a low heat for another minute or two then
transfer to an oven-proof casserole.
Now "dust" the meat.
The beast way to do this is to put some flour into a freezer bag, add the meat and shake then tip it
all into a sieve. Shake again and you will have nicely coated meat with not too much flour sticking
to it. Heat a little more oil and butter in the frying pan and when it is very hot fry the meat until
brown on all sides, transfer the meat to the casserole followed by the parsley, basil, pepper and
the juniper berries. Now add enough water and wine, about one to two cups.
Casserole for one and a half hours but do check occasionally, maybe adding a little more hot liquid
and to prevent the meat from over-cooking. Just before serving I usually stir in a little, one or two
spoons of cream. It makes all the difference!
Mashed potatoes and any vegetable are fine to serve with this casserole, but even better would be
to serve this with our home made red cabbage.
Never be tempted to buy what is sold in supermarkets as red cabbage.

title: Slow Roasted Shoulder of Lamb
story: This will take time, possibly 2-3 hours. So relax and pour yourself a glass of wine. Start by setting your oven to 150. You need:
ingredients: pepper as well as the garlic.
method: one shoulder of lamb with a bit of extra meat on it! This would be enough for 7-8 people but you can buy half shoulders and that is just right for two.
3 sprigs each of rosemary and thyme
2-3 cloves of garlic, crushed
salt and freshly ground pepper and a little olive oil

some potatoes and 1 onion Of course if you roast a small, or half a shoulder, you have to reduce the ingredients! Cover the sides and the bottom of a deep-sided roasting tin with a bit of olive oil. Peel and slice the onion and the potatoes and layer those with some salt and pepper in the bottom of the tin. Now with a sharp knife make a few "slashes" in to the top surface of the lamb. Crush only the leaves of the rosemary and thyme and mix with a little olive oil and some salt and Then all you have to do is to spread this mixture in to the "slashes" and lay the meat on top of the potatoes add a little water and cover with tin foil. Transfer to the over and roast for two hours. Remove the foil and continue roasting for one more hour until the meat is nice and brown and everything looks just right. Roast shoulder of lamb. Appreciated by all of us. Sunday 2nd July 2017

title: Pollo al Chilindron
story: Or simply, Chicken with Peppers and Tomatoes. His is a recipe from the north of Spain and from the Basque country. I found it on the Spice Mountain website, but like almost always I have "adapted " it to my taste, not too much just a little here and there! You need: a few portions of chicken depending on for how many people you cook.
ingredients: 2-3 cloves of garlic peeled and crushed
2 yellow and 2 green peppers sliced in to wide strips
method: and some olive oil
dust the chicken portions very lightly with flour
in a heavy pot or casserole fry the bacon nice and brown
add the chicken and fry this also until it is nicely brown
at this point add a little more olive oil , add the onion cook for a few minutes until just cooked but not brown
now follow with the sliced pepper, garlic, tomatoes, thyme and the paprika.
pour in the wine and you could find that you need a little boiling water too.
Bring things back to the boil and lower the heat to a gentle simmer.
simmer for 30-40 minutes or until the chicken is thoroughly cooked Serve it with freshly baked baguette, a green salad and of course a nice cold Pino.

title: Hare or Rabbit
story: My favourite recipe for Hare or Rabbit start by making the marinade You need:
ingredients: a few sprigs of fresh thyme
a few black and white pepper corns
a handful of smoked bacon bits
a glass of good red wine
method: Cut the hare or rabbit into portions and using a deep dish cover the meat
with the marinade and keep in the refrigerator overnight.
You also need:
chicken stock made from a cube
Next day start with frying the carrots in a little oil and butter for 10 minutes,
and transfer to an oven- prove casserole.
Fry the bacon and also add this to the casserole.
Now take the meat out of the marinade ( save the marinade) and dry it
with kitchen-roll. Dust the meat with a mixture of flour and a little salt.
Fry the meat in the remaining bacon fat until nice and brown and again
add this to the casserole.
Pour a little chicken stock into the frying pan and cook off any residue still
in the pan. ( this holds all the flavour and cannot be wasted)
Pour in the liquid from the pan and enough stock and red wine to almost cover the meat and casserole at 180
for 1 ½ hours or until the meat is tender.
When the meat is tender remove it from the casserole and keep it warm.
To the remaining liquid add two tablespoons of brandy or gin and, most importantly,
Don't be put off by the look of the marinade it will add lots of flavour to the gravy and
it is accentual that you do!
Let the gravy reduce a little and add the cream and the crushed juniper berries.
Cook the gravy gently for a few minutes and taste it to adjust the salt and pepper.
To serve, strain the gravy over the meat.
I usually roast potatoes with this meal and serve it with sauerkraut or homemade
red cabbage.
Of course a good red wine is essential!
The dessert that goes very well with this dish is of course "Rote Grutze"
with vanilla ice-cream.

title: Birnen, Bohnen und Speck
story: or Pears Beans and Bacon. This is a contribution to Lotti-Oma and originates from the old Hamburg kitchens of the past. My family came from different parts of Germany and so I only was introduced to dishes like this after meeting Lotti-Oma. It is rather unusual to say the least...............but after trying it for the first time in her flat I must say that I quite liked it...................but then I eat anything once just to see! For two people you would need:
ingredients: some herb de province ( about a teaspoon full )
1 or maybe two handfuls of smoked bacon lardons
method: The cooking of this dish could not be simpler: melt some butter and gently cook the onion.
Now add the beans, the herbs ,some pepper ( no salt as later on you will add the bacon).
Enough boiling water to cover the beans , bring to the boil and then simmer until the beans are soft
and almost cooked now add the bacon. Half the pears and with their skins on lay those on the top
and continue to simmer until the pears are soft.
Serve this dish with potatoes simply cooked and salted water.
As you can see, and to my surprise, Walter really liked this dish.
So here is to Lotti-Oma and the good old Hamburg recipes.!

title: Steckrueben
ingredients: a handful of smoked bacon lardons.
30 Minutes before the meal is ready add the smoked bacon.
method: Omi cooked this after the war when there was very little food.
But she always found a way and this is a very tasty recipe that filled
us up and also kept us warm.
Give it a go and see.
On this photo there is one ingredient missing and that is:
You also need:
Pork, one to two big pork chops
Prepare the vegetable as shown in the photo.
Melt a little butter in a large pot and add the onions, gently fry until they are just transparent and
add the swedes and pork and enough boiling water to cover the vegetable.
Bring this to the boil and cook for 25 minutes.
Time to put the potatoes in and cook over a medium heat until everything is soft.
Take out the pork and cut in to slices.
Check and add pepper and salt if needed.
Chop the leek very finely.
Transfer everything into a large serving dish and sprinkle the uncooked leek over
the top.
This is a very simple one pot dish and is very good to eat in the winter.

title: Rabbit Stifado
story: Rabbit Stifado ( Greek rabbit stew with onions) After finding this recipe on the Spice Mountain websites and cooking it for the first time I discovered that it is very hard to decide what the amount of a "generous dash of red wine vinegar" actually is. By the second cooking, of this otherwise very nice dish, I had adjusted everything very slightly and was very pleased with the result. So here it goes: You need
ingredients: 1 rabbit, jointed, and a hand-full of smoked bacon
4 teaspoons of tomato puree 1 tsp of ground cumin
1 heaped teaspoon of cinnamon 1 table spoon of brown sugar
method: 1/4 of a bottle of a good red wine 1 tablespoons of "Herbs de Provence"
2 cloves of garlic, crushed about half of a small cup of olive oil
1 tablespoon of red wine vinegar it is also possible that you need some boiling water
Begin with soaking the onion for 2hours in cold water, or you can boil them for2 minutes then drain
and plunge in ice-cold water. This makes the peeling a lot easier. But all this is not necessary
and simply peeling will do fine.
Dust the meat with plain flour.
Heat the oil adds the bacon and after 4 minutes add the Rabbit, fry until everything is nicely brown.
Put all the ingredients, except the onions, in to a large heavy pot with a good thick base and mix
well.
Bring this to the boil and then reduce to a low heat, cover and leave to bubble away
for about one hour.
Check occasionally and add some boiling water if you feel that it is needed.
The sauce should be nice and thick once the Stifado is cooked.
After the first hour add the peeled onions and simmer for another hour or so.
Always keep an eye on the liquid and add water (boiling) if needed.
When the dish is ready you can add a hand-full of chopped parsley.
I serve this dish with "Orzo" a rice-shaped pasta very often used in Greek restaurants.
Follow the cooking instructions.
A freshly baked baguette is nice for mopping-up the rest of the gravy!
Of course you need to make a nice fresh salad topped with Feta cheese.
And if you like to go totally Greek serve everything with nice cold Retsina!

title: Beef Stew & Parsley Dumplings
story: Beef Stew and Parsley Dumplings Very English and very good! One of my favourite winter dishes. Preheat the oven to 170.
ingredients: 1 ¼ lb. Chuck steak cut into 3cm x 3cm cubes
¼ lb. carrots peeled and sliced
¼ lb. turnips cut into small chunks
a bit of dripping or butter
¾ pint of water / a little nice red wine
1 beef stock cube dissolved in boiling water
a handful of smoked bacon cut into lardons
a bay leaf / a few sprigs of thyme
method: To make the stew:
Dust the meat with flour and melt some butter and a little oil in a frying pan and fry the bacon and
the meat until nice and brown and transfer to your casserole.
Now fry the onion, like always making sure that they only cooked and do not get too
dark and brown.
Add those also to the casserole and fry the rest of the vegetable for about 5-10 minutes and after
you transferred the vegetables add all the rest of the ingredients.
Cover the casserole with some silver-foil and a lid and cook in the oven for about 1 ½ -2 hours.
To make the dumplings:
Sift the flour into a basin. Stir in the suet, salt, a little white pepper and the parsley.
Mix this to soft dough with some very cold water and form into balls.
20 minutes before the casserole would be ready arrange the dumplings on the top
and finish cooking in the oven.
Serve with a glass or two of red wine!

title: Tinker's Pie
story: This is the perfect "leftover" dish. It is possible to use almost any meat left over from roasted chicken, lamb, turkey, and rabbit. You can freeze the meat and simply defrost it before you cook this dish at
ingredients: 1 small onion chopped and a little crushed garlic
a few slices of bacon cut in to "lardons"
a handful of chopped parsley and of course salt and pepper
method: You need: 1 sheet of readymade pastry I think puff pastry is the best for this pie.
The leftover meat totally defrosted.
chicken stock made from a cube. Use as much of this as you need to make a
creamy sauce.
about one to two tablespoons of double or clotted cream
First make the chicken stock.
Next heat a little butter or oil in a frying pan and add the bacon.
Fry the bacon until it is nice and brown and then add the onion and if you like a bit of crushed garlic
Fry until the onions are just cooked and add
the mushrooms and continue frying for one to two minutes.
Drain the liquid that has formed in the pan to your stock and keep
mushrooms and bacon warm.
Now heat a little butter in a saucepan and add some flour and mix well.
When the butter is absorbed by the flour gradually add some stock stirring all the time
over a medium heat until the mixture is smooth and creamy.
At this point add the meat and the parsley, bacon, mushrooms and cream too the sauce,
taste to see if salt is needed, then add as much pepper as you feel
the dish requires.
Lastly put the mixture in an ovenproof pie dish and cover it with the pastry then brush with
a little of the beaten egg and bake at 190 for as long as it need to get nice and golden brown,
maybe 30 minutes or a little longer.
Serve this dish with a green vegetable or a green salad.

title: Rouladen Rolladen
story: This again is a recipe cooked for generations in my family, but is also cooked all over Germany in different variations. I think two Rouladen is just about right for each person. For two:
ingredients: 4 slices of beef olives, nice and thin.
A large onion peeled and sliced.
method: Smoked back bacon cut into strips.
Polish gherkins also cut into strips.
Dijon mustard
Start with spreading a little mustard on each of the slices
Next put a little of all the other cutup ingredients on each slice of the beef not
forgetting salt and the peppers of course.
Now start rolling the Rolladen up as shown in the picture, taking care not to lose any
of the filling and fasten carefully with string.
It is possible to obtain string especially made for cooking from any kitchen-shop.
Next heat butter and rapeseed oil in a heavy bottomed, large pot and when the
fat is very hot add the Rolladen.
The meat should get nicely brown on all sides.
This will take quite some time, and every time you turn the meat around add some
boiling water.
Once you are happy that the colour is just right add enough boiling water
to almost cover the meat and cook on a low heat for about 1-1/2 houres.
The colour in the photo is just about right and so is the water level during cooking.
I serve this dish with simply cooked potatoes and a variety of vegetables.
Red cabbage is also very nice to serve with Rolladen.
Usually a good red wine or cold Lager is to be recommended for this dish.

title: Beef Stroganoff
story: Beef Stroganoff comes in very many variations, I quite like this one and I have just added gherkins for extra flavour, and also be course this dish is basically Russian. But like always I have also "adjusted" the recipe just a little, here and there. This meal serves four.
ingredients: two to three polish gherkins cut into slices
Salt and black and white pepper to taste
method: about 110ml stock beef if possible but vegetable or chicken is fine
150ml brandy ?? this sounds a bit too much I think, I certainly use a lot less
Heat a frying pan until very hot and add ½ of the butter
and when the butter is hot add the onion and fry until just softened.
Now add the mushrooms and cook for 2-3 minutes and then add the
tomato puree, mustard, and paprika and cook again for a few minutes.
Lastly add the stock, bring to the boil and then reduce the heat and simmer for 3-4 minutes.
In a separate frying pan heat the remaining butter, then when the butter is very hot
add the beef and fry quickly until very nicely brown but not too long
keeping the meat pink and not fried to "Well done".
Now add the brandy.
The recipe now asks to "carefully allow the pan to flambé ".
I have never done this so at this point you are on your own.
But try not to burn the house down!!
Now add the cream fraiche to the mushroom mixture and then lastly
add the beef and gherkins.
Heat through, and add salt and pepper to taste and sprinkle with parsley.
I would serve this with simple boiled rice.

title: Rundstuck Warm
story: This is a very simple and easily prepared dish and is cooked in North Germany for family celebrations be course once it is cooked in the morning it is then very easy to serve as an informal evening meal. You need:
ingredients: a nice portion of a leg of pork
one or two onions and maybe 2-3 cloves of garlic
method: and some rapeseed oil
Begin with rapping salt, pepper and paprika into the meat and place it into a
high-sided roasting tin.
Chop onions, tomatoes and the garlic fairly small and sprinkle around the meat.
Add a small cup water to the roasting tin and sprinkle a little oil over the meat.
I roast the meat according to the instructions given on the packing, and found
that it always gives the best results.
After the roasting time remove the meat from the tin and allow it to cool for the rest of the
day until it is needed in the evening, and then when totally cold cut it into slices.
The cooking juices are of course needed for the gravy.
It is best to drain the liquid into a jug, it makes making the gravy easier.
Follow the method I almost always use................Melt a little butter in a cooking pot
and add some plain flour and when the flour is absorbed add the cooking juices slowly.
Don't forget to keep stirring all the time until you have a nice creamy sauce.
Should the gravy look a little too pale just add a little sauce-browning. This is perfectly
acceptable and is a very useful thing to have in your kitchen anyway, but be careful and
taste the gravy be course the browning contains salt.
To serve.
Put one or two slices of meat on each plate with some freshly baked baguette
and a few polish gherkins. Now reheat the gravy to a very hot temperature and pour some
over the meat on each of the plates.
Cold Lager goes very well with Rundstuck-Warm.

title: Moroccan Chicken or Lamb
story: Moroccan Chicken/or Lamb with Couscous and black rice. This originates from the "Hairy Bikers" a little altered by me. It serves four or two if very hungry.
ingredients: 275ml chicken stock ( I use more, as much as 300-350ml)
salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 chicken breasts ( make sure they are not too small )
2 teaspoons of ground cinnamon ( I use three)
2 teaspoons of clear honey ( I only use one)
a bunch of coriander (I use parsley)
some Couscous cooked according to instructions
method: 1 teaspoon of ground ginger ( I use two or even better3cm of fresh ginger finely grated ) a handful of dried apricots or prunes or both ( I would use a little more ) You also need: (I also cooked some black rice in salted water as an extra option ) The meal is served with a dish of plain yoghurt . (in my case like always "Total ") As an extra I made salad from 2 chicories 2 mandarins Greek yoghurt and a teaspoon of sugar.
Put the chicken stock the onion, garlic, salt and pepper into a large saucepan and boil for 5-10 minutes or until the liquid has reduced a little.

Add the chicken or lamb, tomatoes, cinnamon, ginger and apricots and/or prunes. Bring everything to the boil lower the heat cover with a lid and simmer for one hour or until the chicken is well cooked or the lamb is tender. Stir in honey and parsley or coriander and reheat. Make the salad drain rice and couscous and serve with cold white wine. Cakes, Biscuits & Desserts Index Cakes Biscuits Desserts

title: Chocolate Espresso Cake
story: When it comes out of the oven the cake should be moist- sticky even-in the middle. As it cools the cake will sink slightly and the crust will crisp. Preheat the oven to 180˚C
ingredients: a small espresso ( about 3 tablespoons of very strong coffee)
method: Line a 21-23 cm spring -form with baking paper, buttering the form lightly to hold the paper in place. Melt the chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of simmering water. As soon as it starts to soften, add the coffee and leave it for two or three minutes. Stir very gently, and then when the chocolate has melted add the butter and stir again until the butter too has melted. Meanwhile, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until stiff then fold in the sugar. Mix the flour and the cocoa-powder. Remove the chocolate from the heat, quickly stir in the egg yolks then slowly and gently fold the melted chocolate into the egg whites. Lastly sift in the flour and cocoa mixture. Stir the mixture with a large metal spoon, taking care not to knock out any air. The mixture should feel light and wobbly. Do not over mix- just enough to fold in the flour. Scoop into the lined tin and bake at 180 for about 25-30 minutes. Leave to cool in tin. Ganache
heat double cream in a heavy based pan do not boil, just hot is fine

remove from heat and add the chocolate leave for 30 seconds, then stir until the chocolate has melted, now add butter and sugar stir in quickly and wait until the mixture has has slightly cooled before covering the cake.

title: Biscuits with Porridge Oats
story: This recipe came originally from Robert to Bobby and I now bake my own variation.
method: ¼ teaspoon of bicarbonate of soda mixed with a tablespoon of boiling water
Cream butter and sugar mix in syrup,
now add flour and oats and lastly add the bicarbonate mixture.
I often add a few sultanas or just bake without anything, just plain.
Line a baking tray with baking paper, form little round balls
and bake at 180 for about 10 minutes.

title: Blackberry & Apple Crumble
story: Blackberry and Apple Crumble This is my variation of an old and much loved crumble. Just give it a try and see. For the fruit filling:
method: sugar to taste
For the crumble:
"Stew" the blackberries very gently over a low heat for 4-5 minutes add the sugar and thicken with
cornflour dissolved in very little cold water.
Peel the apples, cut in to smallish bits and cook gently with the sugar until the apples are
soft but not completely cooked. Sometimes you will need to add a little water ad this point.
Mix the fruits and set aside to cool. This can be done the day before you make the crumble.
Just cover the fruit with cling-film to prevent it from drying out.
For the crumble mix the flour with the baking-powder and the salt plus the sugar.
Rub-in the butter and when you have the consistency of breadcrumbs you can add the milk if you
think it is needed. ( I do be course it make a softer crumble )
Cover the dish with cling-film and keep in the fridge for at least 30 minutes or overnight.
All you need to do the next day, or when you are ready to serve, is to sprinkle the crumble
over the fruit and bake at 160 until the fruit is very hot and the crumbles look nice
and golden.
Serve with cream or ice-cream.
This is a very nice crumble, I promise.

title: Chocolate Mousse
story: This is my favourite chocolate mousse and can be made the day before it is needed. It keeps perfectly well over night in the fridge but can also be frozen for at least three months. Remove it from the freezer 2 hours before serving. It is nice if served with a plain home-made biscuit.
method: Melt the chocolate the usual way and when almost melted add 25g of unsalted butter
Separate the eggs and beat the yolks lightly
Beat the egg-whites until stiff and add the icing-sugar spoon by spoon
Whip the cream until it is nice and fluffy
Mix the egg-yolks into the melted chocolate followed by the cream and lastly gently mix in the egg-white and icing-sugar mixture
spoon into serving glasses or in freezer containers

title: Chocolate Muffins
story: Ingredients for 48 very small Muffins:
ingredients: 1 melt the two chocolates together, the usual way
4 to this add the melted chocolate and stir
5 now fill very small muffin-cases and bake for 12-15 minutes.
method: Method
Preheat oven to 180
2 sieve the flour, baking powder, cocoa and sugar into a large bowl and mix well
3 beat egg, oil, milk and vanilla together and add to the dry ingredients and stir
until well combined
I also add at this point an extra hand full chopped chocolate.
Large muffin cases can also be used all it takes is a few more minutes baking time.

title: Lemon Yoghurt Cake
story: This is one of Marry Berry's best cakes, and I just add three times as much lemon zest as she recommends and one extra egg with nice results. You need a 20cm cake tin. A spring form is the best to use. Grease the tin with butter and line the base with baking paper. You need:
method: 225g Greek yoghurt, I use "Totall" it is simply the best you can buy zest of 3 lemons For the icing about 100g of icing- sugar and enough lemon juice to make a nice smooth icing Preheat the oven to 180.
Cream the butter and sugar and the egg yolks together until smooth add the yoghurt and lemon zest and beat again until smooth, lastly gently fold in the flour
whisk the egg-whites to a soft peak and carefully fold in to the cake-mixture then turn it into the prepared cake tin

bake for 1- 1 ¼ hours or until the cake is well risen and firm to touch I think this is a little too long and would recommend checking it often. It is best to let the cake cool in the tin and then turn it upside down, remove the baking-paper and when it is cool cover it with the lemon -icing using a palette knife. Marry likes to keep this cake in a fridge. In my house the cake never last long enough for that!!

title: A Swirly Chocolate Shortbread
story: For the first shortbread you need:
method: For the first shortbread sift together the flour salt and sugar and rub in the butter.
This is best done in a food- processor. Knead a little cover with cling-film and place in the fridge
For 30 minutes
For the second shortbread you need:
You also need 100g of plain dark chocolate, chopped, with a minimum 60% of cocoa solids.
Follow the same steps as for the first shortbread and chill again for 30minutes.
Preheat the oven to 150.
Now roll out the two mixtures into a rectangular shape about 1cm thick and lay the dark
on top of the white one and sprinkle with the chopped chocolate.
Carefully roll the shortbread into a Swiss-roll. Slice the roll into 1cm biscuits and bake on a lined tray
for about 20-25 minutes.
Don't worry if the chocolate sticks out of the roll these biscuits, or better cookies, are "rustic" rather
than elegant.

Of course there are very may possibilities and ways in which you can arrange or shape
those layers of shortbread.
Here is that one of them.
In this case I did not used the chopped chocolate.

title: Stem Ginger Shortbread
story: Line the baking-tin with baking-paper (use a little butter to make it stick) Heat oven to 150 c
ingredients: 8 balls of stem ginger in syrup dried and finely chopped
method: Measure the flour, butter, sugar, and corn-flour into a food-processor
and whizz until the mixture comes together.
Tip on to a lightly floured worktop and knead in the chopped ginger.
Press dough in to lined tin and using the back of a spoon level the surface.
Sprinkle with demerara sugar and bake for 40 minutes.

title: Everybody's Favourite Apple Cake
story: I found this recipe at least 40 years ago inside a "Springform" bought in Karstadt in Hamburg and have baked it almost constantly. Like always I have "adjusted" it especially after I came across the fantastic "Apple-Cake and Coffee" sold in every Pub in Amsterdam. In Holland there is always a little Cinnamon in apple cake and very often a few sultanas. Bake at 170 for 40-50 minutes. The following ingredients are enough for two cakes using two 18-20cm Springforms.
ingredients: a handful of sultanas / a little cinnamon
one by one followed by the lemon rind and juice.
method: The rind of 2 ½ lemons / and 1 table spoon of juice
also Bramley apples as many as you need
Cream the butter and sugar together and when the mixture is light and fluffy add the eggs,
Lastly add the corn-flour and self-raising flour.
Divide the mixture between two cake tins and sprinkle with cinnamon and sultanas
and top with the peeled and cut apples.
When cutting the apples it is important not to cut the apple-quarters completely
through!
Strait after baking sprinkle the cake with a little sugar.
In Holland or Germany this cake would be served with lovely whipping-cream.
But it is of course also very nice with custard of ice-cream.
The cake is nice cold but can be reheated and served as an apple-pie.

title: Lemon Biscuits
ingredients: 2 table-spoons finely grated rind of lemon
method: Icing-sugar and lemon juice to make icing.
cream the icing sugar and the butter together
mix in the lemon rind and the juice
add flour and corn-flour
form little round balls and place on a baking sheet
bake at 160-170 for 5,6 minutes and after cooling cover with lemon icing if you like

title: Marble Cake, Marmorkuchen
story: Preheat oven to 170 and bake at 150 for about 1 hour. Cake tin bought at M&S. You Need:
ingredients: 250g sugar also: 50g of very good cacao
4 medium eggs separated 30g sugar and again a little milk
¾ of a teaspoon of vanilla paste
method: the grated rind of 1 lemon
and some whole milk
Begin by creaming butter and sugar together and when the texture is very light and creamy add
the vanilla paste and the 4 egg-yolks, cream again and now also add a little salt and the
lemon rind.
Mix the flour and the corn-flour together and und slowly, spoon by spoon, mix the two flours into
the beaten butter.
At this point add enough milk to make the mixture nice and creamy, but not too runny.
It's best now to beat the egg-whites until nice and firm and fold into the cake mixture.
Transfer 1/3 of this into a new bowl and add the 50g of cacao and 30g of sugar mix well.
You need now to make sure that this dark mixture is not too dry by adding more of the milk.
Now butter your cake tin and dust with a little flour.
Fill the baking-tin first with a layer of the light mixture followed by a layer of the dark
and finish with another layer of light.
To achieve the " marble effect " you simply insert a fork and with a twisting movement
mix the two colours up.
This cake goes very well with a cap of tea, but is also very good with nice strong coffee.

title: Chocolate Orange Drizzle Cake
story: This recipe was given to Netty by Ann and then landed in my folder. I have baked it many times and sometimes exchange the oranges with Lemons. I also split the cake and fill it with Orange or Lemon Marmalade. I am afraid that I can never resist covering the cake with melted milk-chocolate.
method: maybe a little milk
Orange or Lemon rind
Orange or Lemon Marmalade
Dark or milk chocolate to cover the cake.
Cream the butter and the sugar add the eggs followed by the flour.
Now add the rind.
Bake at 160 for 40-45 minutes.
Heat the a little of the Orange or Lemon juice with a little sugar
and let it develop into a syrup.
When the cake has cooled drizzle it with the syrup and then when it is completely cold cover
it with melted chocolate.

title: Frozen Lemon Dessert
story: This is a very refreshing dessert and nice after an otherwise "heavy" meal.
method: finely grated rind of 4 lemons and the juice of 2
place the egg-yolks into a bowl and whisk, gradually adding the sugar until the mixture becomes pale and fluffy
add the lemon rind and the juice and beat again
whisk the cream until it becomes thick but not too stiff now fold the cream and the yoghurt into the egg mixture using a metal spoon

finally whisk the egg-whites until stiff and fold in carefully so that not too much air is lost Place the mousse a freezer for at least twelve hours, but this mousse can be frozen month ahead. Remember to take it out of the freezer about 45minutes before serving. This will serve 8, and is nice if accompanied by home-made biscuits. This dessert is very easy to make and keeps in the freezer for up-to 3 month or even longer.

title: Stuffed Peaches
ingredients: A nice dessert and also one of Netty's favourites.
4 nice ripe peaches but not too soft
method: This serves four. preheat the oven to 180
butter an ovenproof dish that is just big enough to hold the 8 peach-halves
cut the peaches in half and remove the stones and also a little of the pulp to make a deep space for the stuffing
add the pulp to the crushed biscuits and stir in the other ingredients
stuff each half and try to mould the mixture into smooth little mounts

put the halves in to the buttered dish and bake in the oven for The peaches are very nice just on their own put can be served with a good vanilla ice cream. Another possibility is to use Digestive biscuits mixed with one or two finely chopped balls of stem-ginger and some double cream. Again just serve with ice-cream or even custard.

title: Lemon Polenta Cake
story: This recipe is from a Tesco web side and is very much like a lemon drizzle cake but with a more granny texture from the Preheat the oven to 180 or fan to 160. You need:
ingredients: ½ tsp of vanilla extract ( I use paste ) >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
method: mm
And the zest of two lemons ( I use 4 lemons)
For the syrup:
the juice of two lemons a little icing sugar and a teaspoon of vanilla paste.
Line a 23cm spring-form with baking-paper.
Cream together butter and sugar until
pale and fluffy.
Combine the flour, almonds, polenta and baking powder in a separate
mixing bowl.
Add a third of the butter mixture to the dry ingredients beat well followed
by one egg followed by more butter and so on until all is well combined.
Finish the batter by beating in the lemon zest.
Spoon the batter into the cake tin and bake for 35-40 minutes.
The cake is ready when the edges have started to shrink away from
the tin and a tester has come out almost clean from the centre of the cake.
While the cake is cooling on a rack make the syrup by mixing together the
lemon juice the icing sugar and the vanilla paste. Bring this to the boil and
remove from the heat.
When the cake is almost cool remove it from the tin, prick the surface and
drizzle with the syrup.
This cake is nice served with vanilla ice-cream or plain Greek yoghurt.

title: Stollen: German Christmas Cake
story: This cake is made, rather unusually, from two different cake mixtures. One is a Brandteig ot Choux and the other one is a Ruehrteig or a Normal cake-mixture. This cake is baked in an unusually long German cake-tin " Stollen form" now easily found in most kitchen shops. Preheat the oven to 170. Before you start the "real baking" it is best to melt the 125g of lard and 75g of shredded suet and cool this for about one hour in the fridge. This mixture should harden a little before you use it later! But now it is best to start with the Choux, for this you need:
method: Bring the water and the butter to the boil . Take the pot of the heat and add all of the flour.
Stir this very quickly until it forms a dough and, bringing the pot back to the cooker,
heat this dough for one minute stirring all the time.
Now quickly transfer the hot dough to a clean bowl wait for two minute and then slowly add the
eggs, one by one. Lastly add the sugar, stir and set aside to cool.
Now for the normal cake mixture, for this you need:
75g shredded suet ........don't forget you have already melted this and it is waiting in your fridge!
and from a German shop some "aroma"
1 Zitrone, I also add the grated rind of one lemon for extra flavour
And later on: 300g of sultanas and 100g of almonds.
Now here we go for the next cake mixture.
This is the " Ruerhrteig " or normal cake mixture.
Transfer the, by now cool fat mixture, (remember it is in you fridge) to a very large
mixing bowl add the two sugars and mix until everything starts to look white and fluffy.
To this add all the ingredients except the eggs and the flour and mix.
It best to take a little time over this and to make sure all the flavours are well mixed in.
Now add the eggs and then bit by bit the four.
I usually tip this mixture on to a work- surface with the choux mixture
followed by the sultanas and the almonds and knead it all until well combined.
From now it's simple.
Fill the cake tin with the mixture and put a baking tray, large enough to cover the
shape of the cake-tin on top turn this over and transfer to the oven.
Reduce the heat to 150 and bake for 10 minutes.
Reduce the heat again, this time to 140 and bake for 50-60 minute.
Be careful and check after 40 minutes...........ever oven is different!
After the cake has cooled for 30 minutes turn it out and brush straightaway
with melted butter and then when completely cool dust with icing-sugar.
I know this is a long job but it's also a very nice Christmas cake that my
Mother and Grand-mother baked every year.
